external_entities.name: customer company
external_entities.description: A customer organization using the invoicing service as a tenant.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant
external_entities.notes: The source describes customer companies as tenants but does not describe an interaction initiated directly by the company.

external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Users are either admins or viewers; they authenticate with an email address, password, and session cookie.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The recipient of an invoice email who can open the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A support employee who operates from the support office network and can open billing-app sessions as customer users.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Each agent signs in with their own account and a one-time code.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users, which manages invoices, customer records, bank details, PDF jobs, and payment pages.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app
processes.notes: The application performs tenant filtering itself and uses shared database and bucket credentials.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: A console available only from the support office network through which support agents can open billing-app sessions as customer users.
processes.source_excerpt: The admin console is reachable only from there

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A renderer that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes PDFs to the PDF bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
processes.notes: It trusts the company ID carried by each job.

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column; the database has no row-level security and is accessed through one database account for all companies.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue carrying PDF render jobs containing a company ID and an invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared bucket where the PDF renderer writes PDFs under a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_stores.notes: The billing app fetches PDFs with one service credential for all companies.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: A customer user uses the billing app and authenticates to it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.notes: The user authenticates with an email address and password and receives a session cookie. There is no second factor for admins or viewers.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie; no second factor

data_flows.name: view payment page
data_flows.description: A payer follows an invoice link and views the payment page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details
data_flows.notes: The payment page asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.data_description: invoice, company name and bank details

data_flows.name: read and write invoice data
data_flows.description: The billing app reads and writes tenant records in the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database
data_flows.notes: The app adds the company filter to each query and connects with one database account for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one database account for all companies
data_flows.data_description: invoices, customers, payout bank details and related tenant records

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue

data_flows.name: take render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads an invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes a rendered PDF to the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID carried by the job.
data_flows.data_description: PDF under the company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one service credential for all companies

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code

data_flows.name: open user session
data_flows.description: The admin console opens a billing-app session as any customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: Actions taken through the session are recorded against the customer user rather than the support agent.

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The customer-company tenant zone in which customer users belong.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud platform zone containing the shared billing app, tenant database, and PDF bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The network from which support agents work and the admin console is reachable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.

assumptions.assumption: The customer company is represented as an external system because the model's ExternalEntity kind values do not include organizations or companies.
assumptions.basis: The source names each customer company as a tenant and a party using the service, but does not describe it as a human or external software system.

assumptions.assumption: The admin console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it an admin console and describes agents signing in to and using it; the model maps a console interface to web.

assumptions.assumption: The tenant database is confidential because it contains invoices, customer records, and payout bank details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF bucket is confidential because it contains rendered PDFs of invoices and associated company and bank details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the renderer writes PDFs to the bucket and that the payment page shows invoices, company names and bank details.
